title: Re-issue of 20261025T1225-c09-review-marangoni (same seed-4 runs and verdict; its seed result wording was read as a failed replication)
summary: Fresh seed 4, T=20000, force scale ampf=0.05 (my reading of the finding's 'force scale 0.05'; the packs do not record WORLD_P), alpha=+20 and alpha=0. alpha=+20: the two seed droplets break up in an early flow-driven burst (t~800-2700, 33 raw splits), the fragments spread as a colony and freeze into a static droplet lattice by t~10000 (a20/seed4/sheet.png); persistent splits 5, max generation 1; the longest net displacements, 3.1 body lengths at speed 0.002, are slow drift during the early spreading, not swimming. alpha=0: 12 splits, 8 persistent, generation 2, max 1.6 body lengths, also a static lattice. The negative result (no self-propulsion, a frozen lattice in every arm) replicates; the claimed increase of persistent splits with alpha=+20 does not on this seed (5 vs 8), because the extra splits are early fragmentation that labkit does not count as persistent.

observations.M: a20/seed4/sheet.png: static lattice from t~10000; motion_seed4.txt: top tracks 3.1 body lengths at speed 0.002 during early spreading (alpha=+20), 1.6 at alpha=0; no droplet swims in the late state

seeds_run.result: pass for the negative M result (alpha=+20 and alpha=0); the division increase with alpha=+20 is absent on this seed (5 vs 8 persistent splits)

controls_run.M: a0/seed4 (alpha=0, same seed and force scale)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I inferred ampf=0.05 from the text. The secondary statement that alpha=+20 raises persistent splits (14/14 vs 10/12) is not reproduced on seed 4 (5 vs 8); alpha=+20 instead fragments the early droplets more (33 vs 12 raw splits). The initial condition is two planted droplets, not noise.
